dimensions.name: Test Execution Fidelity
dimensions.description: Judge whether the substantive Tester and final workflow outputs clearly and faithfully explain the exact bounded test evidence that was recorded, including its target and execution limits.

levels.1: Does not identify the bounded test evidence, describes a materially different execution, or makes an unsupported real-test claim.
levels.2: Identifies the general test area but omits important execution details or blurs the controlled dummy boundary.
levels.3: Accurately identifies the bounded target and result with at most minor presentation omissions.
levels.4: Precisely identifies the target, single bounded invocation, result, evidence source, and dummy limitation in an immediately verifiable form.

examples: Low quality: The backend tests passed, with no target, invocation boundary, or limitation.
High quality: The output names the exact target and one controlled test_runner event, then states that it was not real pytest.
dimensions.deterministic_boundary: The deterministic layer already establishes whether the exact tool event and target exist; this dimension judges how faithfully and usefully the outputs communicate that evidence.

dimensions.name: Outcome Accuracy
dimensions.description: Judge whether the run's substantive outputs classify results consistently with the preserved evidence and distinguish Pass, Blocked, denied, simulated, and real outcomes without contradiction.

levels.1: The stated outcome contradicts the evidence or converts a blocked, denied, or simulated event into real success.
levels.2: The outcome is directionally plausible but ambiguous, internally inconsistent, or missing a material distinction.
levels.3: The outcome is correct and unambiguous, with only minor explanatory gaps.
levels.4: Every material outcome is accurately classified and tied to concrete evidence, including denied attempts and limitations.

examples: Low quality: Treating natural-language Pass text as a tool result.
High quality: Separating the dummy Tester Pass, current approval, and controlled tracker response from real pytest or external-service success.
dimensions.deterministic_boundary: The deterministic layer checks exact event facts; this dimension judges the semantic accuracy and consistency of the narrative conclusions.

dimensions.name: Evidence Coverage
dimensions.description: Judge whether the outputs surface the material evidence needed to review the run, including role outputs, tool evidence, approvals, scope, failures, limitations, and unresolved gaps.

levels.1: Omits most material evidence or invents evidence that is absent.
levels.2: Provides the main outcome but omits one or more important evidence categories or leaves key gaps implicit.
levels.3: Covers the material evidence categories and explicitly identifies unavailable evidence or skips.
levels.4: Organizes complete, source-grounded evidence so a reviewer can verify the result immediately, with every gap and limitation clearly labeled.

examples: Low quality: Reporting only that the workflow passed.
High quality: Reporting role outputs, approvals, exact controlled events, changed paths, protected state, preserved failures, and unmeasured budgets.
dimensions.deterministic_boundary: The deterministic layer validates required fields and sequences; this dimension judges completeness, organization, and review usefulness.

dimensions.name: Readiness Recommendation Quality
dimensions.description: Judge whether the run's recommendation follows from the bounded evidence, names the next safe action, and separates workflow readiness from unmeasured backend, deployment, security, and holdout behavior.

levels.1: The recommendation is missing, contradicts the evidence, or claims broad readiness unsupported by the run.
levels.2: The recommendation is directionally reasonable but vague, weakly justified, or poorly scoped.
levels.3: The recommendation follows from the evidence and includes a clear scope limitation.
levels.4: The recommendation is concise, actionable, explicitly evidence-based, and clearly separates measured readiness from every material unmeasured risk.

examples: Low quality: Everything is production ready.
High quality: The recorded workflow is suitable as a development baseline, while real pytest, deployment health, security completeness, and holdout generalization remain unverified.
dimensions.deterministic_boundary: The deterministic layer cannot judge whether a recommendation is calibrated, useful, and proportionate to the evidence.
